How you're experiencing it ▼

Same drink, different conditions, different aroma. These don't change the chemistry — they change how much of it reaches you.

How you sense smell ▼

Not every nose sensation is smell. Menthol, camphor, vinegar, mustard oil and capsaicin also trigger the trigeminal nerve in your nose and mouth, which reports cool, burn or sting alongside the aroma. You can feel these with no sense of smell at all. Tell the wheel what you felt.

    Select a star to read it. Click empty space, or press Escape, to clear.

    Chemistry and Taxonomy are computed live from the same note, compound, and citation graph the wheel uses. Nothing here is a separate or simplified dataset. Geography plots recorded cultivation coordinates only. Notes without a recorded origin collect in an explicit tray rather than getting a guessed position. Embodied only places a note once you tag it this session, so nothing is asserted as a fixed fact about the note itself.

    Map positions reflect the pre-Columbian Exchange framing used throughout: where a plant was cultivated or first used by humans before 1492 European contact, not necessarily where it is grown commercially today.

    Known origin Approximate · — nothing in your experience yet; add notes on the Wheel · toggle groups · Pre-Columbian Exchange framing. Click markers to select notes.
    Flavor notes are the fruit. Plants bloom upward, fungal lineages root downward, and ecological visitors float beside the stems without joining them.

    Placement: represented APG IV lineage, not age. Order names are an optional reading layer.

    Biologically placeable plant and fungal notes, organized by Kingdom → Order → Family. Plantae grows above the trunk flare while Fungi forms the downward root system. Honey’s bee floats beside the base—and optional pollinator/dispersal icons sit inside family florets—without ancestry lines, because ecological relationships are not taxonomy. Represented plant Orders gather under high-level APG IV lineage groups; vertical position does not encode when a lineage appeared. Process descriptors and umbrella aroma terms remain available in the Wheel but are intentionally omitted here. Berry* is culinary shorthand spanning Ericaceae, Grossulariaceae, Lythraceae, and Rosaceae—not a botanical family.
